byType.label: Hired you once, never came back
byType.explain: Happy customers who used you one time. They'll need you again — the question is whether they remember your name.

byType.label: Quotes nobody answered
byType.explain: You sent a price, they never said yes or no, and the follow-ups stopped. Most of these people didn't say no — nobody asked again.

byType.label: Quotes filed away
byType.explain: Quotes that got archived without a yes. Archiving cleans up your screen — it also means nobody will ever follow up.

byType.label: Due for service again
byType.explain: Work that comes around on a clock — pump-outs, sweeps, washes, clean-ups. They're due, and they don't know it.

byType.label: The next job nobody offered
byType.explain: The natural follow-on to work you already did — stump grinding after a removal, sealing after a pour. Never offered.

byType.label: Asked for changes, never got a new quote
byType.explain: They wanted the job with a tweak. These are some of the warmest people in your whole file.

byType.label: Add-ons left on the table
byType.explain: They took the main job and passed on an option you offered. The job is done — the option is still a good idea.

byType.label: Regulars who went quiet
byType.explain: Customers who used you on a rhythm and then stopped. Usually nobody asked why.

byType.label: Said yes, never got scheduled
byType.explain: Work you already won that never made it onto the calendar. This is the fastest money in your business.

welcome.text:
Derek, it's Quiet Accounts. In the last two years, 50% of your quotes never got a yes or a no. All told, 1,024 quotes, $1.3M, are sitting quiet. Nobody said no to that money; nobody asked.

Here's the first note, going out in your name:

Hi Grace,

It's Derek at Corriveau Tree Service. You got a price from us last October for the stump grinding.

We never heard back. Is it still something you want done?

If you went another way, that's fine. Just reply "pass" and I'll close it out.

Derek

Reply OK and the first 324 go out Tuesday, April 14, then the rest of your 1,347, newest first, each one about their own job. It's one pass through your list: the last notes go out May 12. Want anything changed? Just tell me what. Nothing goes out until you say OK.

When someone wants the work, I'll text you their name, number and what they said. Just reply:
BOOKED 2400 (the amount) when you book one
NO if it's dead
BUSY until May 5 if you're slammed — we'll wait
PAUSE to stop everything

Worth a call from you (we don't email these): 212 with only a phone number, $216k in all. Biggest first: Ryan Patel (603) 959-3537 (lot clearing, $5,050); Kevin Fischer (603) 959-9791 (pruning, $5,025); Julie Reyes (603) 959-9741 (oak removal, $3,975).

You pay $250 for each job that books, never more than $1,000. Nothing books, you owe nothing.

ok.reply: Done — the first notes go out Apr 14. When someone wants the work, you'll get a text with their name and number.
